courses.title: Automate Real Work with n8n
courses.tagline: Nebula runs on spreadsheets, a flaky CRM and hope. Every week, hours vanish into copy-paste work that a machine should do. Over five modules, you become the person who fixes that — by shipping real, working automations.
courses.goal: Design, build, debug and maintain real n8n workflows — from a silent Slack alert to clean, reliable data pipelines.
learn: Build n8n workflows that start from a trigger, guard against bad data, alert the right people, and prove the work was done.
Clean, reshape and de-duplicate messy data with expressions, Set and Filter nodes before it ever reaches your CRM.
Route work with IF and Switch, merge branches back together, and call REST APIs that paginate and rate-limit.
Make workflows survive failure with retries and error workflows, keep AI under control, and prove it all in a capstone build.

modules.title: Foundations: Your First Working Workflow
modules.pain: The lead alert workflow died at 2:07 AM. 40 leads lost before anyone noticed.

lessons.title: Workflow anatomy
notes: A workflow starts with a trigger — no trigger, no run.
One trigger event starts one execution, which passes through the nodes in order.
Actions do the visible work, and only run when an execution reaches them.

lessons.title: Data & items
notes: Each row is one item; every node runs once per item.
Tidy field names once, early, so every later node reads clean names.
A Filter is a guard: items that fail it stop there.

lessons.title: Build the lead alert
notes: The shape to remember: trigger → clean → guard → alert.
A guard only protects what comes after it.
Green means the node ran — read its response to know the work was done.

modules.title: Data Transformation: Taming Messy Data
modules.pain: A 500-row export with mixed date formats, duplicate IDs and blank emails. Ana wants it CRM-ready.
modules.lead_in: You can now move data safely from a trigger to an action. Next you learn to change it on the way: clean messy fields, reshape each item and remove duplicates — inside the same trigger → guard → action shape.

lessons.title: Expressions
notes: Expressions run for each item, on the fly.
Trim and lower-case values before comparing them.
“Undefined” almost always means a misspelled or missing field name.

lessons.title: Reshaping with Set
notes: Set renames, adds and reshapes fields — it never stops an item.
Fill defaults in one place, upstream.
Normalise before you default, or one value turns into two.

lessons.title: Cleaning real data
notes: The order: normalise → guard → guard → write.
Dedup compares values, so they must share one format first.
Count every rejection, and be able to explain each one.

modules.title: Logic, Branching & APIs
modules.pain: VIP and standard orders, digital and physical — and a CRM API that paginates and rate-limits.
modules.lead_in: So far your pipelines run in a straight line. Next they branch: different paths for different cases, merging them back together, and talking to outside systems through their APIs.

lessons.title: Conditional logic
notes: Filter drops items; IF and Switch route them.
IF has two paths, Switch has many.
Always give Switch a path for “everything else”.

lessons.title: Merging branches
notes: Append stacks items; Combine pairs them by a shared field.
Merge waits for both inputs.
Normalise the matching field first, then count.

lessons.title: Talking to APIs
notes: A request has a method, a URL, authentication and a body.
Read the status code first: 200, 401, 404, 429.
Expect pagination and rate limits.

modules.title: Reliability & AI
modules.pain: Duplicate invoices, silent failures, and 200 tickets a day that an AI could triage.
modules.lead_in: Next comes what happens when things break: catching errors, retrying safely, and putting AI in the loop without losing control.

lessons.title: When things break
notes: Failures are temporary or permanent.
Retry the temporary ones; continue past bad items and keep them.
Anything retried must be safe to run twice.

lessons.title: Error workflows
notes: An error workflow starts with an Error Trigger.
A good alert says what failed, where, and links to the run.
Use Stop and Error when nothing broke but the result is wrong.

lessons.title: AI in the loop
notes: Use a model for reading, rules for exact tests.
Ask for a fixed set of answers and validate them.
A person approves anything that cannot be undone.

modules.title: Bigger Workflows: Reuse, Code & Files
modules.pain: The same cleaning steps copied into five workflows, a tax rule no node can express, and invoices that arrive as PDFs.
modules.lead_in: Your workflows now survive failure and can use AI. Next they grow up: reusable sub-workflows, a few lines of your own code when no node fits, and files.

lessons.title: Sub-workflows
notes: A sub-workflow does one job for a parent workflow.
Build once, reuse everywhere.
Small parts are easier to read and test.

lessons.title: The Code node
notes: Use a node if one exists; code if none does.
Choose the mode: each item, or all items.
Always return items, and keep secrets out of code.

lessons.title: Files and binary data
notes: An item can carry fields and a file.
Extract from File: file → items. Convert to File: items → file.
Check the file is still attached after each node.
